current_episode.title: The Power of Personal Development: Proving Every Doubter Wrong with Steve Mitchell #190

guest.titre_secondaire: Motivational Speaker and Personal Development Coach
guest.bio_context: Steve Mitchell left school labeled as a daydreamer with ADHD (undiagnosed at the time), became a trainee chef, then joined the army for six years as an infantryman serving in Colchester, Northern Ireland, Cyprus, the Middle East, Canada, America, and Egypt. After leaving the army to prioritize fatherhood, he built a career as a musician and entertainer, performing with bands including Ebonfly and The Ley Lines alongside major artists, while also working as a chef and in property maintenance. He has been sober for 10 years (since New Year's Day 2017) and is now focused on personal development coaching and establishing his business Release the Best You while relocating to France with his wife Donna.

pending_qa.q: What role did his wife Donna play in Steve Mitchell's entrepreneurial journey?
pending_qa.r: Mitchell credits his wife Donna as the lynchpin to his entire entrepreneurial success. She supported him when he decided to join the army, moved with him, and started her own doggy daycare business 17 years ago, which became the stable foundation allowing him to pursue various ventures. She has literally kept them afloat during difficult times and told him when he was very low, 'I don't have enough energy for the two of us, you need to sort yourself out.'

pending_qa.q: What major career transitions has Steve Mitchell made after leaving the army?
pending_qa.r: After leaving the army, Mitchell pursued music seriously, performing as a singer-songwriter with multiple bands including Ebonfly and The Ley Lines. Ebonfly performed with major artists like Girls Aloud, Mark Ronson, Take That, Daniel Beddingfield, and Charlotte Church. The Ley Lines toured with The Levellers and recorded in their studio. After 13 years with The Ley Lines, Mitchell ended the band a couple of months before the interview to focus on health, fitness, and his business Release the Best You.

pending_qa.q: What is Steve Mitchell's current purpose and mission in life?
pending_qa.r: Mitchell's mission statement is to be as fit, strong, and healthy as possible mentally, physically, and emotionally so he has the best chance of living as long as possible to see his youngest grandchild turn into an adult and create a meaningful legacy. He emphasizes that purpose must be bigger than oneself, and his driving factor is about his grandchildren needing their grandfather around for as long as possible to pass on knowledge and lived experience.

pending_qa.q: How long has Steve Mitchell been sober and how did this affect his career decisions?
pending_qa.r: Mitchell will have been 10 years free from alcohol and drugs as of New Year's Day 2027. Being sober changed his perspective on the rock and roll lifestyle associated with touring bands, as the payoff of being on stage for an hour and a half in front of thousands of people was no longer worth the time in the van, lack of sleep, and missing weekends with his wife and grandchildren. This realization contributed to his decision to end The Ley Lines after 13 years.

pending_qa.q: What risk did Steve Mitchell take with his property investment that paid off significantly?
pending_qa.r: When Mitchell and Donna moved to their current property about seven years ago, the mortgage was five times more than the property they were leaving. However, they identified the potential to earn 10 times more money. Mitchell converted a barn into a doggy daycare center, a stable into an office, and another stable into a grooming salon, working from 5 a.m. to 1 a.m. in rain, wind, and snow. Looking back now at what they started with compared to what they have built is 'crazy,' he says.

pending_qa.q: How long has Steve Mitchell been married to his wife Donna?
pending_qa.r: Mitchell and Donna have been married for 34 years. He proposed to her in an unconventional way while they were looking out over the bay of Weston-super-Mare in their flat, telling her 'I suppose we better get married now then' because they could not get an army house unless they were married. They married between his phase one and phase two army training.
